doc.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025

title: Learning saxophone and other instruments
summary: Levy learned the chromatic scale on diatonic harmonica, then saxophone at 19, and other instruments, which deepened his understanding of Coltrane.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: And you know I also used to play sax. I played tenor, alto, soprano, and flute. And that was one of the things – I talk about this in the book that one of the other ways that I learned about music was learning music through the instruments. You know. And I just, after I learned harmonica, and you know after about oh I don't know, three or four months of playing harmonica, that’s when I figured out how to play the chromatic scale on it which nobody had ever done on the diatonic before. And that’s a long story. But I started sounding very good and playing in all different keys on one, and not just the

standard blues stuff. And then I thought well maybe I could learn some other instruments and of course Coltrane, like I said, was like a saint to me. You know. It’s like gee if I could learn how to play the saxophone, wow. That would be like a sacred instrument that I could actually learn how to play it. So someone lent me a horn and I started to learn how to play that when I was 19. And then the same thing happened with other instruments. And I was never a great saxophone player but I learned so much about the workings of the horn and I got the Sigurd Rascher book you know, Top Tones.

I’m sure you do. And you know the whole way that the overtone series works through the horn and it’s not a linear instrument, and then listening to Coltrane with that knowledge was like oh my God, that’s what he’s doing, and hearing all the stuff Pharoah Sanders and Albert Ayler were doing and all that stuff. Like I started understanding it from the inside out and not just having it be this sort of mind-blowing thing that I didn’t – that was just impressions. I was understanding it. And the same thing happened with all sorts of other string instruments I learned how to play and percussion instruments. So my learning process has been very multi-faceted. And at the same time as that was happening in the early and mid-‘70s I started getting into quote world music before it had a name. I was just fascinated – actually Coltrane, believe it or not – was the impetus for that. There was this one tune and I know you know this tune, it was from that Prestige album called “The Last Train” where he played “Lover” at like 500 miles an hour. Have you heard that recording?
